How a smart device works

A heart monitor or smartwatch turns a sensor reading into information someone can use. An EV charger measures and controls how power flows. All rely on circuits that collect signals and software that decides what to do with them.

From calibrated instrument to field trial

  1. Semester 1 Smart measuring instrument

    Design an instrument and calibrate its readings.

  2. Semester 2 Connected device

    Build a working device on a circuit board you designed.

  3. Semester 3 Embedded signal processing

    Build a board that can process a real-world signal.

  4. Semester 4 Real-time motor control

    Build a controller that balances, steers or drives a motor.

  5. Semester 5 On-device AI

    Run a model locally on a product powered by Linux.

  6. Semester 6 A 10-unit pilot batch

    Build a secure product and produce its first 10 units.

  7. Semester 7 A field trial

    Build a device that solves a user’s problem, then test it in the field.

  8. Semester 8 Engineering work

    Spend 16–20 weeks working in a company or the Product Studio.

Circuits, firmware and edge AI

Hardware

Design circuits and printed circuit boards. Work with ARM and RISC-V microcontrollers, FPGAs and design for manufacturing.

Software

Program in C, C++ and Python. Work with real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, device drivers and device security.

Embedded intelligence

Process signals, control hardware and run machine learning models on devices.

Where it leads

Explore work in embedded systems and firmware, edge AI, embedded Linux, IoT products, and automotive and EV electronics. The skills also support building a hardware startup.

For those who want the detail

The sequence introduces measurement and circuit design before embedded computing and control. Later projects test the device as a product through security checks, pilot manufacturing and a field trial. Individual practical assessments record what each student can demonstrate on their own.

Common questions

What does Electronics and Computer Engineering cover?

You design the hardware, write the software that runs on it and learn to test them together.

Does the degree prepare me for software roles?

The curriculum includes programming, data structures, operating systems and software engineering. These are foundations for software roles.
